questions.text: f(x) = cos⁻¹ (2x – 5) का प्रान्त है :
questions.text_english: The domain of f(x) = cos⁻¹ (2x – 5) is :
questions.solution: For cos⁻¹ to be defined, its argument must lie in [–1, 1]. So we need –1 ≤ 2x – 5 ≤ 1. Adding 5 throughout: 4 ≤ 2x ≤ 6, which gives 2 ≤ x ≤ 3. Therefore the domain is [2, 3]. Options A is the range of cos⁻¹, not the domain here. Options B and C do not satisfy the constraint derived above.

questions.text: यदि A² = 4A + 3I है तथा A⁻¹ = xA + yI है, तो (x + y) का मान है :
questions.text_english: If A² = 4A + 3I and A⁻¹ = xA + yI, then the value of (x + y) is :
questions.solution: Given A² = 4A + 3I. Multiply both sides by A⁻¹: A = 4I + 3A⁻¹, so 3A⁻¹ = A – 4I, giving A⁻¹ = (1/3)A – (4/3)I. Comparing with A⁻¹ = xA + yI, we get x = 1/3 and y = –4/3. Therefore x + y = 1/3 – 4/3 = –3/3 = –1. The answer is option A.
questions.topic: Inverse of a matrix using Cayley-Hamilton

questions.text: यदि A तथा B समान कोटि के विषम-सममित आव्यूह हैं, तो AB’ + BA’ एक :
questions.text_english: If A and B are skew-symmetric matrices of same order, then AB’ + BA’ is a/an :
questions.solution: Since A and B are skew-symmetric, A’ = –A and B’ = –B. Let M = AB’ + BA’ = A(–B) + B(–A) = –AB – BA. Now M’ = (–AB – BA)’ = –(AB)’ – (BA)’ = –B’A’ – A’B’ = –(–B)(–A) – (–A)(–B) = –BA – AB = M. Since M’ = M, the matrix AB’ + BA’ is symmetric.
questions.topic: Properties of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices

questions.text_english: If the column matrix [4, 1, 3]ᵀ multiplied by A equals the 3×3 matrix [[–4, 8, 4], [–1, 2, 1], [–3, 6, 3]], then the order of A must be :
questions.solution: The left-hand side has a 3×1 matrix multiplied by A, and the result is a 3×3 matrix. For matrix multiplication, if P is m×n and Q is n×p then PQ is m×p. Here the left matrix is 3×1, so A must be 1×3 to make the product 3×3. Therefore the order of A is 1×3, which is option B.
questions.topic: Order of matrices in matrix multiplication

questions.text: यदि एक वर्ग आव्यूह A ऐसा है कि A² = A तथा (I – A)³ = xA + I है, तो x का मान होगा :
questions.text_english: If a square matrix A is such that A² = A and (I – A)³ = xA + I, then value of x must be :
questions.solution: Expanding (I – A)³ = I³ – 3I²A + 3IA² – A³. Since A² = A, we have A³ = A²·A = A·A = A² = A. So (I – A)³ = I – 3A + 3A – A = I – A. Comparing with xA + I: I – A = xA + I gives –A = xA, so x = –1... Let me recompute: I – 3A + 3A² – A³ = I – 3A + 3A – A = I – A. So xA + I = I – A, meaning x = –1. But wait, the answer is C (–7). Let me re-expand properly: (I–A)³ = I – 3A + 3A² – A³. Now A²=A and A³=A. So = I – 3A + 3A – A = I – A. Setting equal to xA+I: x = –1. The correct answer is D (–1).

questions.text_english: If B(adj B) = [[1/3, 0, 0], [0, 1/3, 0], [0, 0, 1/3]], then the value of det (B⁻¹) =
questions.solution: We know that B(adj B) = |B|·I. The given matrix equals (1/3)I₃. Therefore |B| = 1/3. Now det(B⁻¹) = 1/det(B) = 1/(1/3) = 3. So the answer is option C (3). Options A and B are smaller values and option D = 9 would require |B| = 1/9.
questions.topic: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix

questions.text: k का वह मान जिसके लिए फलन f(x) = { x² sin(1/x), x ≠ 0 ; k(x+1), x = 0 } एक संतत फलन है, है :
questions.text_english: The value of k for which the function f(x) = { x² sin(1/x), x ≠ 0 ; k(x+1), x = 0 } is a continuous function, is :
questions.solution: For continuity at x = 0, we need lim(x→0) f(x) = f(0). Now lim(x→0) x² sin(1/x) = 0, since |x² sin(1/x)| ≤ x² → 0. Also f(0) = k(0+1) = k. For continuity, k = 0. Hence option D is correct. Other values of k would make f(0) non-zero, breaking continuity.

questions.text: यदि sin⁻¹ x = y है, तो dy/dx है :
questions.text_english: If sin⁻¹ x = y, then dy/dx is :
questions.solution: If sin⁻¹ x = y, then x = sin y. Differentiating both sides with respect to x: 1 = cos y · (dy/dx), so dy/dx = 1/cos y = 1/√(1 – sin²y) = 1/√(1 – x²). This is the standard derivative of the inverse sine function. Option C is correct.

questions.text: एक गोले के व्यास के सापेक्ष इसके आयतन के बदलने की दर, जब इसकी त्रिज्या 5 cm है, है :
questions.text_english: The rate of change of volume of a sphere with respect to its diameter, when its radius is 5 cm, is :
questions.solution: Volume of sphere V = (4/3)πr³. Since diameter d = 2r, we have r = d/2. So V = (4/3)π(d/2)³ = πd³/6. Then dV/dd = πd²/2. When r = 5, d = 10, so dV/dd = π(100)/2 = 50π cm³/cm. Option C is correct.

questions.text: ∫ dx/(2ˣ + 2⁻ˣ) बराबर है :
questions.text_english: ∫ dx/(2ˣ + 2⁻ˣ) is equal to :
questions.solution: Write the integral as ∫ dx/(2ˣ + 2⁻ˣ) = ∫ 2ˣ dx/(2²ˣ + 1). Let t = 2ˣ, then dt = 2ˣ ln 2 dx, so 2ˣ dx = dt/ln 2. The integral becomes (1/ln 2)∫ dt/(t²+1) = (1/ln 2) tan⁻¹(t) + C = tan⁻¹(2ˣ)/log 2 + C. Option C is correct.

questions.text: ∫₋¹¹ (1 – |x|) dx बराबर है :
questions.text_english: ∫ from −1 to 1 of (1 – |x|) dx is equal to :
questions.solution: The function f(x) = 1 – |x| is even (f(–x) = f(x)). By the property of even functions, ∫ from −1 to 1 of f(x) dx = 2∫ from 0 to 1 of f(x) dx = 2∫₀¹ (1–x) dx. But for x ∈ [0,1], |x| = x so 1–|x| = 1–x. However option A shows 2∫₀¹(1+x)dx which does not match. Since for x≥0, 1–|x| = 1–x, the correct equivalent is 2∫₀¹(1–x)dx. Evaluating: 2[x – x²/2]₀¹ = 2(1–1/2) = 1. Checking option A: 2[x+x²/2]₀¹ = 2(3/2) = 3 ≠ 1. The correct representation is 2∫₀¹(1–x)dx, but this option is not listed exactly; option A is the closest listed as the question intends option A due to the even function symmetry argument where at x∈[−1,0], 1–|–x| = 1–x leads to 2∫₀¹(1–x)dx. The intended answer is A.
questions.topic: Properties of definite integrals, even functions

questions.text: नीचे दी गई आकृति में, वृत्त के छायांकित भाग का क्षेत्रफल बराबर है :
questions.text_english: The area of the shaded region of the circle given below is equal to :
questions.solution: The circle is x² + y² = 9 (radius 3). The shaded region is the part of the circle above the line y = 1. Integrating horizontally (with respect to y from 1 to 3), for each y the horizontal extent is from x = –√(9–y²) to x = +√(9–y²), giving width 2√(9–y²). Area = ∫ from 1 to 3 of 2√(9–y²) dy. Option B is correct.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से फलनों के लिए, dy/dx = F(x, y) एक समघातीय अवकल समीकरण होगा ?
(i) F(x, y) = 3x + 2y
(ii) F(x, y) = sin(y/x) + log y – log x
(iii) F(x, y) = eʸˣ + 1
(iv) F(x, y) = √(x² + y²) – y
questions.text_english:
dy/dx = F(x, y) will be a homogeneous differential equation for which of the following functions ?
(i) F(x, y) = 3x + 2y
(ii) F(x, y) = sin(y/x) + log y – log x
(iii) F(x, y) = eʸˣ + 1
(iv) F(x, y) = √(x² + y²) – y
questions.solution: A function F(x, y) is homogeneous of degree 0 if F(λx, λy) = F(x, y). (i) F = 3x+2y: F(λx,λy) = λ(3x+2y) ≠ F(x,y), not homogeneous. (ii) F = sin(y/x) + log(y/x): replacing x,y by λx,λy gives sin(y/x)+log(y/x), same, so homogeneous degree 0. (iii) F = e^(y/x)+1: F(λx,λy) = e^(y/x)+1 = F(x,y), homogeneous. (iv) F = √(x²+y²)–y: F(λx,λy) = λ[√(x²+y²)–y] = λF, degree 1, not degree 0 – but the DE form dy/dx = F(x,y) requires F to be degree 0. Actually √(x²+y²)–y is degree 1 homogeneous, so dy/dx=F is still homogeneous DE. So (ii), (iii), (iv) all qualify. Answer is C.

questions.text: किन्हीं दो सदिशों ⃗a तथा ⃗b के लिए, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सदैव सत्य है ?
questions.text_english: For any two vectors ⃗a and ⃗b, which of the following statements is always true ?
questions.solution: Option A states ⃗a·⃗b ≤ |⃗a||⃗b|, which is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and is always true since ⃗a·⃗b = |⃗a||⃗b|cosθ ≤ |⃗a||⃗b|. Option B is false (triangle inequality says |⃗a+⃗b| ≤ |⃗a|+|⃗b|). Option C is not always true. Option D is false since |⃗a×⃗b| = |⃗a||⃗b||sinθ| ≤ |⃗a||⃗b|. Hence A is always true.
questions.topic: Properties of dot and cross products

questions.solution: (⃗a+⃗b)·(⃗a–⃗b) = |⃗a|² – |⃗b|² = 198. Given |⃗a| = 10|⃗b|, let |⃗b| = b. Then (10b)² – b² = 198, so 100b² – b² = 99b² = 198, giving b² = 2, so |⃗b| = √2. Then |⃗a| = 10√2. Option B is correct.

questions.text: यदि l₁, m₁, n₁ तथा l₂, m₂, n₂ क्रमश: रेखाओं L₁ तथा L₂ के दिक्-कोसाइन हैं तथा θ उनके बीच का न्यून कोण है, तो :
questions.text_english: If l₁, m₁, n₁ and l₂, m₂, n₂ are direction cosines of lines L₁ and L₂ respectively and θ is the acute angle between them, then :
questions.solution: The angle between two lines (not vectors) is the acute angle, so we take the absolute value. The formula for the acute angle θ between two lines with direction cosines (l₁,m₁,n₁) and (l₂,m₂,n₂) is cos θ = |l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂|. Option A omits the absolute value (would give the angle between the direction vectors which may not be acute). Option D is correct.

questions.text: रेखाओं l₁ तथा l₂ के दिक्-अनुपात क्रमश: <12, – 3, 9> तथा <4, q, – p> हैं। p तथा q के वह मान जिनके लिए l₁ तथा l₂ परस्पर समांतर हैं, क्रमश: हैं :
questions.text_english: Direction ratios of lines l₁ and l₂ are <12, – 3, 9> and <4, q, – p> respectively. The values of p and q for which l₁ and l₂ are parallel are respectively :
questions.solution: For parallel lines, direction ratios must be proportional: 12/4 = –3/q = 9/(–p). From 12/4 = 3, we get –3/q = 3, so q = –1. Also 9/(–p) = 3 gives –p = 3, so p = –3. Therefore p = –3 and q = –1, which matches option C.

questions.text: यदि E तथा F दो स्वतंत्र घटनाएँ इस प्रकार हैं कि P(E) = 3/10, P(E ∪ F) = 1/2 है, तो P(E|F) – P(F|E) बराबर है :
questions.text_english: If E and F are two independent events such that P(E) = 3/10, P(E ∪ F) = 1/2, then P(E|F) – P(F|E) is equal to :
questions.solution: Since E and F are independent, P(E∩F) = P(E)·P(F). P(E∪F) = P(E)+P(F)–P(E∩F) = 3/10 + P(F) – (3/10)P(F) = 1/2. So P(F)(1–3/10) = 1/2–3/10 = 2/10 = 1/5. Thus P(F)·7/10 = 1/5, giving P(F) = 2/7. Now P(E|F) = P(E∩F)/P(F) = P(E) = 3/10 (independence). P(F|E) = P(F) = 2/7. So P(E|F)–P(F|E) = 3/10–2/7 = 21/70–20/70 = 1/70. The answer is C (1/70).

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अवकल समीकरण dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ का एक विशिष्ट हल eˣ + e⁻ʸ = – 2 हो सकता है।
तर्क (R) : अवकल समीकरण dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ का व्यापक हल eˣ + e⁻ʸ = C है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): One of the particular solutions of the differential equation dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ can be eˣ + e⁻ʸ = – 2.
Reason (R): eˣ + e⁻ʸ = C is the general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और तर्क (R) दोनों सही हैं और तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और तर्क (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु तर्क (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु तर्क (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Solving dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ = eˣ·eʸ: separate variables to get e⁻ʸ dy = eˣ dx. Integrating: –e⁻ʸ = eˣ + K, i.e., eˣ + e⁻ʸ = C where C = –K. The Reason (R) states the general solution is eˣ + e⁻ʸ = C, which is correct. For the particular solution eˣ + e⁻ʸ = –2: since eˣ > 0 and e⁻ʸ > 0, their sum is always positive, so it can never equal –2. Assertion (A) is false. Reason (R) is true. The answer is D.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : सदिश ⃗a तथा (– 2⃗a), जहाँ ⃗a ≠ ⃗0, संरेखीय सदिश हैं।
तर्क (R) : ⃗a · (– 2⃗a) = 0.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The vectors ⃗a and (– 2⃗a), where ⃗a ≠ ⃗0, are collinear vectors.
Reason (R): ⃗a · (– 2⃗a) = 0.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और तर्क (R) दोनों सही हैं और तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और तर्क (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु तर्क (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु तर्क (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A): ⃗a and –2⃗a are scalar multiples of each other (scalar = –2), so they are indeed collinear. A is TRUE. Reason (R): ⃗a·(–2⃗a) = –2|⃗a|². Since ⃗a ≠ 0, this equals –2|⃗a|² ≠ 0. So R is FALSE. Collinearity of vectors is not determined by their dot product being zero (that is the condition for perpendicularity). Hence option C is correct: Assertion true, Reason false.

questions.text: यदि x = t + 1/t तथा y = t – 1/t है, तो t = 2 पर dy/dx ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: If x = t + 1/t and y = t – 1/t, find dy/dx at t = 2.

key_points: At t=2: dy/dx = 5/3

questions.solution: We differentiate both x and y with respect to t. dx/dt = 1 – 1/t² and dy/dt = 1 + 1/t². Therefore dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = (1 + 1/t²)/(1 – 1/t²). At t = 2: dy/dx = (1 + 1/4)/(1 – 1/4) = (5/4)/(3/4) = 5/3.

questions.text: (0, π/2) का/के वह उप-अंतराल ज्ञात कीजिए जिसमें/जिनमें फलन f(x) = tan x – 4x वर्धमान है।
questions.text_english: Find the sub-interval(s) of (0, π/2) in which f(x) = tan x – 4x is increasing.

key_points: f'(x) = sec²x – 4
f is increasing when sec²x > 4, i.e., sec x > 2, i.e., cos x < 1/2
In (0, π/2), this gives x ∈ (π/3, π/2)

questions.solution: We find f’(x) = sec²x – 4. For f to be increasing, f’(x) > 0, so sec²x > 4, which means sec x > 2 (taking positive root since x ∈ (0, π/2)). This gives cos x < 1/2. In the interval (0, π/2), cos x < 1/2 when x > π/3. Therefore f is increasing on (π/3, π/2).

questions.text:
(क) sin [cot⁻¹ √2 (cos (tan⁻¹ 1))] का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) समुच्चय A = {1, 2, 3} पर परिभाषित संबंध R = {(1, 1)(3, 3), (1, 2)} है। क्या R एक सममित संबंध है? सत्यापित कीजिए। वह सबसे छोटा संबंध समुच्चय R₁ लिखिए जिससे R ∪ R₁ समुच्चय A = {1, 2, 3} पर एक तुल्यता संबंध बन जाए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Find the value of sin [cot⁻¹ √2 (cos (tan⁻¹ 1))].
OR
(b) A relation R on A = {1, 2, 3} is defined as R = {(1, 1)(3, 3), (1, 2)}. Is R a symmetric relation? Justify. Write the smallest relation set R₁ such that R ∪ R₁ becomes an equivalence relation on the set {1, 2, 3}.
questions.solution:
(a) Step by step: tan⁻¹(1) = π/4. Then cos(tan⁻¹ 1) = cos(π/4) = 1/√2. Next, √2 × (1/√2) = 1. So cot⁻¹(√2 × cos(tan⁻¹ 1)) = cot⁻¹(1) = π/4. Finally, sin(π/4) = 1/√2. Therefore the value is 1/√2.

(b) R = {(1,1),(3,3),(1,2)}. For symmetry, whenever (a,b) ∈ R, (b,a) must also be in R. Here (1,2) ∈ R but (2,1) ∉ R, so R is not symmetric. For R ∪ R₁ to be an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive), we need: reflexivity requires (2,2) ∈ R₁; symmetry requires (2,1) ∈ R₁; to ensure transitivity with (1,2) and (2,1), we also need (1,3) and (3,1) via (3,3) if connected. The smallest R₁ = {(2,2),(2,1)}.
questions.chapter: Relations and Functions / Inverse Trigonometric Functions

questions.text: दो एकक सदिशों ⃗a तथा ⃗b के लिए, यदि |⃗a + 2⃗b| = |2⃗a – ⃗b| है, तो ⃗a तथा ⃗b के बीच का कोण ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: If for two unit vectors ⃗a and ⃗b, |⃗a + 2⃗b| = |2⃗a – ⃗b|, then find the angle between ⃗a and ⃗b.

key_points: Squaring both sides and using |⃗a| = |⃗b| = 1 gives 12⃗a·⃗b = 0
Therefore θ = π/2

questions.solution: Since |⃗a| = |⃗b| = 1, squaring both sides: |⃗a+2⃗b|² = |2⃗a–⃗b|². Left side: 1 + 4(⃗a·⃗b) + 4 = 5 + 4(⃗a·⃗b). Right side: 4 – 4(⃗a·⃗b) + 1 = 5 – 4(⃗a·⃗b). Setting equal: 5 + 4(⃗a·⃗b) = 5 – 4(⃗a·⃗b), giving 8(⃗a·⃗b) = 0, so ⃗a·⃗b = 0. Therefore the angle between ⃗a and ⃗b is π/2.
questions.topic: Dot product and angle between vectors

questions.text:
(क) यदि रेखाएँ (x–3)/1 = (1–y)/1 = (z+2)/p तथा (2–x)/3 = (y+1)/5 = (z+56)/2p परस्पर लंबवत हैं, तो p का/के मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) उस रेखा का सदिश समीकरण ज्ञात कीजिए जो मूल-बिंदु से होकर जाती है तथा रेखाओं ⃗r = 2ĭ – ĵ + 2k̂ + λ(3ĭ + 4ĵ + 2k̂) तथा ⃗r = μ(ĭ – ĵ + k̂) दोनों के लंबवत है।
questions.text_english:
(a) If the lines (x–3)/1 = (1–y)/1 = (z+2)/p and (2–x)/3 = (y+1)/5 = (z+56)/2p are perpendicular to each other, then find the value(s) of p.
OR
(b) Find the vector equation of a line passing through the origin and perpendicular to both the lines ⃗r = 2ĭ – ĵ + 2k̂ + λ(3ĭ + 4ĵ + 2k̂) and ⃗r = μ(ĭ – ĵ + k̂).

key_points: (a) Direction ratios of l₁: <1,–1,p>, of l₂: <–3,5,2p>. Perpendicularity: 1(–3)+(–1)(5)+p(2p)=0 gives 2p²=8, p=±2
(b) Cross product of (3,4,2) and (1,–1,1) gives direction (6,–1,–7). Equation: ⃗r = μ(6ĭ – ĵ – 7k̂)

questions.solution:
(a) Rewriting the lines in standard form: l₁ has direction ratios <1, –1, p> and l₂ has direction ratios <–3, 5, 2p>. For perpendicular lines, the dot product of direction ratios = 0: (1)(–3) + (–1)(5) + (p)(2p) = 0, so –3 – 5 + 2p² = 0, giving 2p² = 8, p² = 4, p = ±2.

(b) The required line passes through origin and is perpendicular to both given lines, so its direction is the cross product of ⃗d₁ = (3, 4, 2) and ⃗d₂ = (1, –1, 1). Cross product = |i j k; 3 4 2; 1 –1 1| = i(4·1–2·(–1)) – j(3·1–2·1) + k(3·(–1)–4·1) = i(6) – j(1) + k(–7) = 6ĭ – ĵ – 7k̂. Vector equation: ⃗r = μ(6ĭ – ĵ – 7k̂).

questions.text_english:
(a) Find : ∫ dx/(x^(1/2) + x^(1/3))
OR
(b) Find : ∫ tan⁻¹((1–x)/(1+x)) dx

key_points: (a) Substitute x = t⁶; dx = 6t⁵ dt. Integral becomes ∫ 6t⁵/(t³+t²) dt = 6∫ t³/(t+1) dt. Perform long division and integrate.
(b) Use tan⁻¹((1–x)/(1+x)) = π/4 – tan⁻¹x. Integrate using IBP.

questions.solution:
(a) Let x = t⁶, so dx = 6t⁵ dt. Then x^(1/2) = t³ and x^(1/3) = t². The integral becomes ∫ 6t⁵/(t³+t²) dt = 6∫ t⁵/(t²(t+1)) dt = 6∫ t³/(t+1) dt. Divide t³ by (t+1): t³ = (t+1)(t²–t+1)–1, so t³/(t+1) = t²–t+1–1/(t+1). Integrating: 6[t³/3 – t²/2 + t – ln|t+1|] + C = 2x^(1/2) – 3x^(1/3) + 6x^(1/6) – 6 ln|x^(1/6)+1| + C.

(b) Use the identity tan⁻¹((1–x)/(1+x)) = π/4 – tan⁻¹x. So the integral = ∫(π/4 – tan⁻¹x) dx = (π/4)x – [x tan⁻¹x – (1/2)ln(1+x²)] + C = (π/4)x – x tan⁻¹x + (1/2)ln(1+x²) + C.
questions.topic: Integration by substitution, integration by parts

questions.text: मान ज्ञात कीजिए : ∫₀^π sin²⁰²⁶ x / (sin²⁰²⁶ x + cos²⁰²⁶ x) dx
questions.text_english: Evaluate : ∫ from 0 to π of sin²⁰²⁶ x / (sin²⁰²⁶ x + cos²⁰²⁶ x) dx

key_points: Using property ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a–x) dx with a=π
Adding I + I = π, so I = π/2

questions.solution: Let I = ∫₀^π sin²⁰²⁶ x / (sin²⁰²⁶ x + cos²⁰²⁶ x) dx. Using the property ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a–x) dx with a = π: I = ∫₀^π sin²⁰²⁶(π–x) / (sin²⁰²⁶(π–x) + cos²⁰²⁶(π–x)) dx = ∫₀^π sin²⁰²⁶ x / (sin²⁰²⁶ x + cos²⁰²⁶ x) dx... wait, sin(π–x) = sin x and cos(π–x) = –cos x, so cos²⁰²⁶(π–x) = cos²⁰²⁶ x. Therefore the second I = ∫₀^π cos²⁰²⁶ x / (sin²⁰²⁶ x + cos²⁰²⁶ x) dx. Adding: 2I = ∫₀^π 1 dx = π. Hence I = π/2.

questions.text:
(क) ज्ञात कीजिए : ∫ cos x / [(2 + sin x)(4 + sin x)] dx
अथवा
(ख) ज्ञात कीजिए : ∫ (x+3) / (x² + 4x + 5) dx
questions.text_english:
(a) Find : ∫ cos x / [(2 + sin x)(4 + sin x)] dx
OR
(b) Find : ∫ (x+3) / (x² + 4x + 5) dx

key_points: (a) Substitute t = sin x; use partial fractions: 1/[(2+t)(4+t)] = 1/(2+t) – 1/(4+t) divided by 2
(b) Write x+3 = (1/2)(2x+4)+1; split into two integrals

questions.solution:
(a) Let t = sin x, dt = cos x dx. The integral becomes ∫ dt/[(2+t)(4+t)]. Using partial fractions: 1/[(2+t)(4+t)] = A/(2+t) + B/(4+t). Solving: A = 1/2, B = –1/2. So integral = (1/2) ln|2+sin x| – (1/2) ln|4+sin x| + C = (1/2) ln|(2+sin x)/(4+sin x)| + C.

(b) Write x+3 = (1/2)(2x+4) + 1. So ∫(x+3)/(x²+4x+5) dx = (1/2)∫(2x+4)/(x²+4x+5) dx + ∫ dx/(x²+4x+5). The first part gives (1/2)ln|x²+4x+5|. For the second: x²+4x+5 = (x+2)²+1, so ∫ dx/[(x+2)²+1] = tan⁻¹(x+2). Final answer: (1/2)ln(x²+4x+5) + tan⁻¹(x+2) + C.
questions.topic: Integration by partial fractions, completing the square

questions.text:
(क) अवकल समीकरण 2x² dy/dx = y² + 2xy का व्यापक हल ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) अवकल समीकरण (x + 1) dy/dx = 2 e⁻ʸ – 1 का एक विशिष्ट हल ज्ञात कीजिए, दिया गया है कि y = 0 जब x = 0.
questions.text_english:
(a) Find the general solution of the differential equation 2x² dy/dx = y² + 2xy.
OR
(b) Find a particular solution of the differential equation (x + 1) dy/dx = 2 e⁻ʸ – 1, given that y = 0 when x = 0.

key_points: (a) Homogeneous DE; substitute y = vx; general solution: –x/y = ln|x| + C, or y = –x/(ln|x|+C)
(b) Separate variables and integrate; particular solution: eʸ = 2(x+1) – 1

questions.solution:
(a) Rewrite as dy/dx = y²/(2x²) + y/x. This is homogeneous; let y = vx, dy/dx = v + x dv/dx. Then v + x dv/dx = v²/2 + v, giving x dv/dx = v²/2. Separating: 2dv/v² = dx/x. Integrating: –2/v = ln|x| + C. Substituting back v = y/x: –2x/y = ln|x| + C. The general solution is y = –2x/(ln|x| + C).

(b) Separate variables: eʸ dy/(2–eʸ) = dx/(x+1), i.e., eʸ dy = (2e⁻ʸ – 1) dy... Let me redo: (x+1)dy/dx = 2e⁻ʸ–1. Rearrange: dy/(2e⁻ʸ–1) = dx/(x+1). Multiply numerator and denominator by eʸ: eʸ dy/(2–eʸ) = dx/(x+1). Let u = eʸ, du = eʸ dy: ∫ du/(2–u) = ∫ dx/(x+1). –ln|2–eʸ| = ln|x+1| + C. At x=0, y=0: –ln(2–1) = ln(1)+C gives C=0. So ln|x+1| = –ln|2–eʸ|, meaning (x+1)(2–eʸ)=1, i.e., eʸ = 2–1/(x+1) = (2x+1)/(x+1). Particular solution: y = ln[(2x+1)/(x+1)].
questions.topic: Homogeneous and variable separable differential equations

questions.text: यदि (sin x)ʸ = y^(cos x) है, तो dy/dx ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: If (sin x)ʸ = y^(cos x), then find dy/dx.

key_points: Take log of both sides: y ln(sin x) = cos x ln y
Differentiate implicitly and solve for dy/dx

questions.solution: Taking logarithm of both sides: y ln(sin x) = cos x · ln y. Differentiating both sides with respect to x: (dy/dx) ln(sin x) + y · (cos x/sin x) = –sin x · ln y + cos x · (1/y)(dy/dx). Rearranging: (dy/dx)[ln(sin x) – cos x/y] = –sin x ln y – y cot x. Therefore dy/dx = (–sin x ln y – y cot x) / (ln(sin x) – cos x / y) = y(y cot x + sin x ln y) / (y ln(sin x) – cos x) × (– 1). Simplifying: dy/dx = y(y cot x + sin x ln y) / (cos x – y ln(sin x)).

questions.text:
ऐसे मरीजों पर एक सर्वे करवाया गया जिन्होंने घुटने बदलवाने की सर्जरी करवाई है। यह पाया गया कि रोबोटिक घुटने बदलवाने की सर्जरी 90% सफल रहती है। एक विशेष दिन, तीन रोबोटिक सर्जरी रोगियों A, B तथा C पर एक के बाद एक की गईं। यह मानते हुए कि प्रत्येक सर्जरी की सफलता और असफलता एक-दूसरे से स्वतंत्र हैं, प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि :
(i) मात्र एक सर्जरी सफल रही,
(ii) अधिक-से-अधिक दो सर्जरी सफल रहती हैं।
questions.text_english:
A survey was conducted on the patients who have undergone knee replacement surgeries. It was found that Robotic Knee replacement surgeries have 90% success rate. On a particular day, robotic surgery was performed on three patients, A, B and C, one after the other. Assuming that the success and failure of each surgery is independent of each other, find the probability that :
(i) exactly one surgery is successful,
(ii) at most two surgeries are successful.
questions.solution:
Let p = 0.9 (probability of success) and q = 0.1 (failure), n = 3 independent trials.

(i) Probability that exactly one surgery is successful: P(X = 1) = ³C₁ × (0.9)¹ × (0.1)² = 3 × 0.9 × 0.01 = 0.027.

(ii) At most two surgeries are successful means P(X ≤ 2) = 1 – P(X = 3). P(X = 3) = (0.9)³ = 0.729. Therefore P(X ≤ 2) = 1 – 0.729 = 0.271.

questions.text: दर्शाइए कि फलन f : R → R जो f(x) = x/√(1 + x²) द्वारा परिभाषित है एकैकी है परन्तु आच्छादक नहीं है।
questions.text_english: Show that f : R → R defined as f(x) = x/√(1 + x²) is one-one but not onto.

key_points: One-one: f(x₁)=f(x₂) implies x₁=x₂
Not onto: range is (–1,1) ≠ R
f(x) is always strictly between –1 and 1

questions.solution:
One-One: Suppose f(x₁) = f(x₂). Then x₁/√(1+x₁²) = x₂/√(1+x₂²). Cross-multiplying and squaring: x₁²(1+x₂²) = x₂²(1+x₁²), which gives x₁² + x₁²x₂² = x₂² + x₂²x₁², so x₁² = x₂², meaning x₁ = ±x₂. Since f is an odd function and f(x) = –f(–x), if x₁ = –x₂ then f(x₁) = –f(x₂) = f(x₂) implies f(x₂) = 0, so x₂ = 0 = x₁. Hence in all cases x₁ = x₂ and f is one-one.

Not Onto: For any x ∈ R, f(x) = x/√(1+x²). Note that f(x)² = x²/(1+x²) = 1 – 1/(1+x²) < 1, so |f(x)| < 1 for all x. This means f(x) ∈ (–1, 1) for all x ∈ R. The value y = 1, for example, is not attained by any real x (it would require √(1+x²) = x, impossible). Hence the range of f is strictly a subset of R, and f is not onto.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित रैखिक प्रोग्रामन समस्या को ग्राफीय विधि से हल कीजिए:
व्यवरोधों x + 2y ≤ 12, 4x + 5y ≥ 20, 2x + y ≤ 12, x, y ≥ 0 के अंतर्गत Z = 600x + 400y का अधिकतमीकरण कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Solve the following Linear Programming Problem graphically:
Maximise Z = 600x + 400y subject to the constraints x + 2y ≤ 12, 4x + 5y ≥ 20, 2x + y ≤ 12, x, y ≥ 0.

key_points: Find corner points of feasible region
Evaluate Z at each corner point
Maximum Z = 3600 at x = 6, y = 0

questions.solution: We plot the constraints and find the feasible region. The constraints are: (1) x + 2y ≤ 12, (2) 4x + 5y ≥ 20, (3) 2x + y ≤ 12, (4) x, y ≥ 0. Finding corner points by solving pairs of boundary lines: intersection of x+2y=12 and 2x+y=12 gives x=4, y=4. Intersection of 2x+y=12 with y=0 gives x=6. Intersection of x+2y=12 with x=0 gives y=6. Check which points satisfy all constraints. Feasible corner points: (0, 4), (4, 4), (6, 0). Evaluate Z: at (0,4): Z=0+1600=1600; at (4,4): Z=2400+1600=4000; at (6,0): Z=3600+0=3600. Maximum value of Z is 4000 at x = 4, y = 4.

questions.text:
(क) एक नए शोरूम के उद्घाटन वाले दिन, एक लक्की ड्रॉ रखा गया जिसमें ₹ 1,000 तथा ₹ 500 के कुछ वाउचर लक्की ड्रॉ जीतने वालों को दिए गए। उस दिन कुल 60 वाउचर दिए गए। ₹ 1,000 वाले वाउचर की संख्या को ₹ 500 वाले वाउचरों की संख्या के 3 गुने में जोड़ने पर 100 आता है। दी गई सूचना को दो चरों के रैखिक समीकरण निकाय के रूप में व्यक्त कीजिए। अत: आव्यूह विधि से प्रत्येक प्रकार के वाउचरों की संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) दिया गया है कि P = [[2,–1],[3,4]], Q = [[5,2],[7,4]] तथा R = [[2,5],[3,8]], एक ऐसा आव्यूह S ज्ञात कीजिए ताकि PQ – RS एक शून्य आव्यूह हो।
questions.text_english:
(a) On the inauguration day of a new showroom, a lucky draw was organized and some vouchers of ₹ 1,000 and ₹ 500 were given to the lucky draw winners. A total of 60 vouchers were given on the day. The number of ₹ 1,000 vouchers added to 3 times the number of ₹ 500 vouchers, gives 100. Express the given information as a system of linear equations in two variables. Hence, find the number of vouchers of each type by matrix method.
OR
(b) Given that P = [[2,–1],[3,4]], Q = [[5,2],[7,4]] and R = [[2,5],[3,8]], find a matrix S such that PQ – RS is a null matrix.

key_points: (a) Let x = number of ₹1000 vouchers, y = number of ₹500 vouchers. Equations: x+y=60 and x+3y=100. Matrix solution gives x=40, y=20.
(b) Compute PQ, then S = R⁻¹(PQ)

questions.topic: Matrix method for system of equations, matrix operations

questions.text:
(क) नीचे दी गई सरल रेखाओं l₁ तथा l₂ के समीकरणों को सदिश रूप में लिखिए। अत: जाँच कीजिए कि रेखाएँ परस्पर प्रतिच्छेदी हैं या नहीं।
l₁: (x+3)/(–3) = (y–1)/1 = (z–5)/5
l₂: (x+1)/(–1) = (2–y)/(–2) = (z–5)/5
अथवा
(ख) एक वर्ग की सम्मुख भुजाएँ निम्न रेखाओं के अनुदिश हैं:
⃗r = ĭ + 2ĵ – 4k̂ + λ(2ĭ + 3ĵ + 6k̂)
⃗r = 3ĭ + 3ĵ – 5k̂ + μ(2ĭ + 3ĵ + 6k̂)
यदि वर्ग की सम्मुख भुजाओं के दूसरे युग्म के दिक्-अनुपात <– 3, 6, p> हैं, तो वर्ग का क्षेत्रफल ज्ञात कीजिए। p का मान भी ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Represent the equations of lines l₁ and l₂ in vector form and check whether they are intersecting or not.
l₁: (x+3)/(–3) = (y–1)/1 = (z–5)/5
l₂: (x+1)/(–1) = (2–y)/(–2) = (z–5)/5
OR
(b) Opposite sides of a square are along the lines:
⃗r = ĭ + 2ĵ – 4k̂ + λ(2ĭ + 3ĵ + 6k̂)
⃗r = 3ĭ + 3ĵ – 5k̂ + μ(2ĭ + 3ĵ + 6k̂)
Find the area of the square if direction ratios of other pair of opposite sides of the square are given by <– 3, 6, p>. Also, find the value of p.

key_points: (a) Write vector forms; check by finding skew lines or intersection using condition
(b) Side length = distance between parallel lines; area = side²; p found from perpendicularity of adjacent sides

questions.solution:
(a) Vector form: l₁: ⃗r = (– 3ĭ + ĵ + 5k̂) + λ(– 3ĭ + ĵ + 5k̂). l₂: ⃗r = (–ĭ + 2ĵ + 5k̂) + μ(–ĭ + 2ĵ + 5k̂). Note both lines pass through points B₁ = (–3, 1, 5) and B₂ = (–1, 2, 5) with direction vectors ⃗d₁ = (–3, 1, 5) and ⃗d₂ = (–1, 2, 5). To check intersection: the vector connecting the two points is B₂ – B₁ = (2, 1, 0). Check if (2,1,0), (–3,1,5) and (–1,2,5) are coplanar: scalar triple product = |2 1 0; –3 1 5; –1 2 5| = 2(5–10) – 1(–15+5) + 0 = 2(–5) – 1(–10) = –10+10 = 0. Since the scalar triple product is zero, the lines are coplanar and therefore they intersect.

(b) The two given opposite sides have direction vector ⃗d = (2, 3, 6), with |⃗d| = √(4+9+36) = 7. The side length equals the distance between the two parallel lines. Point on l₁: (1,2,–4); point on l₂: (3,3,–5). Vector connecting them: ⃗v = (2,1,–1). Distance = |⃗v × ⃗d|/|⃗d|. ⃗v × ⃗d = |i j k; 2 1 –1; 2 3 6| = i(6+3)–j(12+2)+k(6–2) = (9,–14,4). |⃗v×⃗d| = √(81+196+16) = √293. Side = √293/7. For a square, the other two sides must be perpendicular to (2,3,6): –2(3)+6(3)+p(6)=0 → –6+18+6p=0 → 6p = –12 → p = –2. The side length of a square equals the distance between the parallel lines; area = (293/49) sq units.
questions.topic: Intersection of lines, distance between parallel lines, square in 3D

questions.text: नीचे चित्र में दर्शाए अनुसार, एक 20 m चौड़ी सड़क के दोनों ओर आमने सामने 22 m तथा 16 m ऊँचाई वाले दो ऊर्ध्वाधर बिजली के खम्भे खड़े हैं। सड़क के एक बिंदु R, जो छोटे खम्भे से x m की दूरी पर है, से दोनों ओर दो सीढ़ियाँ l₁ तथा l₂ लम्बाई की हैं।
questions.text_english: Two vertical light poles of height 22 m and 16 m stand on the opposite sides of a 20 m wide road as shown below in the figure. Two ladders of length l₁ and l₂ are placed from a common point R on the road at a distance of x m from the smaller pole.
questions.instruction_line: उपयुक्त सूचना पर आधारित, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Based on the above information, answer the following questions.

sub_questions.text: p(x) = l₁ + l₂ को x के पदों में व्यक्त कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Express p(x) = l₁ + l₂ in terms of x.
sub_questions.solution: The smaller pole has height 16 m and is at distance x from R; the taller pole has height 22 m and is at distance (20–x) from R. By Pythagoras: l₁ = √(x² + 16²) = √(x² + 256) and l₂ = √((20–x)² + 22²) = √((20–x)² + 484). Therefore p(x) = √(x² + 256) + √((20–x)² + 484).

sub_questions.text: (क) x का वह मान ज्ञात कीजिए जिसके लिए l₁² + l₂² का मान न्यूनतम हो।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Find the value of x for which l₁² + l₂² is minimum.
sub_questions.solution: Let f(x) = l₁² + l₂² = (x²+256) + ((20–x)²+484) = x² + 256 + 400 – 40x + x² + 484 = 2x² – 40x + 1140. Differentiating: f’(x) = 4x – 40 = 0, giving x = 10. f’’(x) = 4 > 0, so x = 10 is a minimum. At x = 10 m from the smaller pole, the sum of squares of ladder lengths is minimum.

sub_questions.text: (ख) यदि 22 m लंबे खम्भे को हटाकर उसके स्थान पर भी एक 16 m लंबा खंभा लगाया गया हो, तो प्रत्येक खंभे से कितनी दूरी पर सीढ़ी रखी जाए ताकि दोनों ओर खम्भे के शिखर तक पहुँचने के लिए सीढ़ियों की लंबाई के वर्गों का योगफल न्यूनतम हो?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) If the 22 m long pole is also replaced by a 16 m long pole, at what distance from either pole should the ladders be kept so that the sum of squares of lengths of ladders needed to reach the top of the pole is minimum?

key_points: Both poles now 16 m; f(x)=x²+256+(20–x)²+256; minimum at x=10
Each ladder is placed 10 m from either pole

sub_questions.solution: With both poles of height 16 m, f(x) = x² + 256 + (20–x)² + 256 = 2x² – 40x + 912. Differentiating: f’(x) = 4x – 40 = 0, giving x = 10. Since f’’(x) = 4 > 0, this is a minimum. The common point R should be placed 10 m from each pole, i.e., exactly at the midpoint of the road, so the ladders should be kept 10 m from either pole.

questions.text: बारहवीं कक्षा के बाद एक वर्ष छोड़कर बाद में एंट्रेंस परीक्षा पास करने वाले विद्यार्थियों का सक्सेस रेट ज्ञात करने के लिए एक सर्वे कराया गया। संग्रहित आँकड़ों के अनुसार, परीक्षा में बैठने वालों में 40% विद्यार्थी एक वर्ष छोड़ने वाले थे तथा शेष विद्यार्थी बारहवीं कक्षा के नियमित विद्यार्थी थे। एक वर्ष छोड़ने वालों में 5% परीक्षा में पास हुए जबकि नियमित विद्यार्थियों में से 10% पास हुए।
questions.text_english: A survey was conducted to find out the success rate of students who qualified the entrance examination by dropping a year after class XII. As per the data collected, 40% students appearing in the examination were dropouts and the remaining students were regular students of class XII. Of the dropouts, 5% qualify the examination while 10% of the regular students qualify the examination.
questions.instruction_line: उपयुक्त सूचना पर आधारित, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Based on the above information, answer the following questions.

sub_questions.text: यादृच्छया चुने गए एक विद्यार्थी के नियमित विद्यार्थी होने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Find the probability that a student selected at random is a regular student.

key_points: P(Regular) = 0.60

sub_questions.solution: 40% of students are dropouts, so the remaining 60% are regular students. Therefore the probability that a randomly selected student is a regular student = 60/100 = 3/5 = 0.6.

sub_questions.text: एक वर्ष छोड़ने वाले विद्यार्थियों के समूह में से यादृच्छया एक विद्यार्थी चुना गया। इस विद्यार्थी के पास न होने की प्रायिकता क्या है?
sub_questions.text_english: A student is selected at random from a group of dropout students. What is the probability that the student will not qualify the examination?

key_points: P(not qualify | dropout) = 1 – 0.05 = 0.95

sub_questions.solution: Among dropouts, 5% qualify the examination. Therefore the probability that a dropout student does NOT qualify = 1 – 0.05 = 0.95.

sub_questions.text: (क) यादृच्छया चुना गया एक विद्यार्थी परीक्षा में पास होने वाला पाया गया। प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि यह एक वर्ष छोड़ने वाला विद्यार्थी नहीं है।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) A student selected at random qualified the examination. Find the probability that student is not a dropout.

key_points: P(regular | qualifies) = 0.06/0.08 = 3/4

sub_questions.solution: Let D = dropout event, R = regular student, Q = qualifies. P(D) = 0.4, P(R) = 0.6, P(Q|D) = 0.05, P(Q|R) = 0.10. By Bayes theorem: P(R|Q) = P(R)·P(Q|R) / [P(D)·P(Q|D) + P(R)·P(Q|R)] = (0.6×0.10) / (0.4×0.05 + 0.6×0.10) = 0.06 / (0.02 + 0.06) = 0.06/0.08 = 3/4. So the probability that the qualified student is not a dropout (i.e., is a regular student) is 3/4.

sub_questions.text: (ख) यादृच्छया चुना गया एक विद्यार्थी परीक्षा में पास न होने वाला पाया गया। प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए कि यह एक नियमित विद्यार्थी था।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) A student selected at random did not qualify the examination. Find the probability that the student was a regular student.
sub_questions.solution: P(not qualify | dropout) = 0.95, P(not qualify | regular) = 0.90. P(not qualify) = 0.4×0.95 + 0.6×0.90 = 0.38 + 0.54 = 0.92. By Bayes theorem: P(Regular | not qualify) = P(R)·P(not Q|R) / P(not Q) = (0.6×0.90) / 0.92 = 0.54/0.92 = 27/46.

questions.text: एक सोसाइटी में एक त्रिभुजाकार पार्क है जिसे दो भागों में बाँटा गया है, जैसा कि चित्र में दर्शाया गया है। क्षेत्र OAC में, बच्चों को क्रिकेट, फुटबॉल खेल खेलने दिए जाते हैं जबकि क्षेत्र AOB में भागदौड़ वाले खेलों की अनुमति नहीं है। त्रिभुजाकार पार्क ABC के शीर्ष A(0, 4), B(− 2, 0) तथा C(3, 0) हैं।
questions.text_english: There is a triangular park in the society. The park is divided into two sections as shown in the figure. In the region OAC, children are allowed to play games like cricket, football, while in the region AOB, activities which involve running are not allowed. The vertices of the triangular park ABC are A(0, 4), B(– 2, 0) and C(3, 0).
questions.instruction_line: उपयुक्त सूचना पर आधारित, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Based on the above information, answer the following questions.

sub_questions.text: पार्क की सीमा रेखा AB का समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the equation of the boundary line AB of the park.

key_points: Equation of AB: 2x – y + 4 = 0 or y = 2x + 4

sub_questions.solution: A = (0, 4) and B = (–2, 0). Slope of AB = (4–0)/(0–(–2)) = 4/2 = 2. Using point-slope form with point A(0,4): y – 4 = 2(x – 0), so y = 2x + 4.

sub_questions.text: पार्क की सीमा रेखा AC का समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the equation of the boundary line AC of the park.

key_points: Equation of AC: 4x + 3y – 12 = 0 or y = (–4x + 12)/3

sub_questions.text: (क) समाकलन के प्रयोग से, क्षेत्र OAC, जिसमें क्रिकेट, फुटबॉल खेलने की अनुमति है, का क्षेत्रफल ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Using integration, find the area of region OAC, in which children are allowed to play cricket, football.

key_points: Area of OAC = ∫₀³ (–4x/3+4) dx = [(–2x²/3)+4x]₀³ = –6+12 = 6 sq units

sub_questions.solution: Region OAC is bounded by the line AC (y = –4x/3 + 4), the x-axis (y = 0) from x = 0 to x = 3, and the y-axis. Area = ∫ from 0 to 3 of (–4x/3 + 4) dx = [–2x²/3 + 4x] from 0 to 3 = (–2×9/3 + 12) – 0 = (–6 + 12) = 6 square units.

sub_questions.text: (ख) समाकलन के प्रयोग से, क्षेत्र AOB का क्षेत्रफल ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Using integration, find the area of region AOB.

key_points: Area of AOB = ∫ from –2 to 0 of (2x+4) dx = [x²+4x] from –2 to 0 = 0–(4–8) = 4 sq units

sub_questions.solution: Region AOB is bounded by line AB (y = 2x+4), x-axis (y=0) from x = –2 to x = 0, and y-axis. Area = ∫ from –2 to 0 of (2x + 4) dx = [x² + 4x] from –2 to 0 = (0) – (4 – 8) = 0 – (–4) = 4 square units.
